school.title: Heap Sort
school.short_summary: Heap sort turns the input into a heap and repeatedly extracts the max.
school.long_summary: Heap sort builds a binary heap from the input and repeatedly removes the largest element to produce a sorted array.
school.simple_explanation: Imagine all elements stored in a pyramid where each parent is bigger than its children; taking the top element and rebuilding the pyramid gives a sorted list.
school.where_its_used: Used in introductory CS courses and anywhere deterministic O(n log n) sorting is needed without extra memory.
school.example: Sorting numbers [4, 1, 3, 2] results in [1, 2, 3, 4] after building and draining the heap.

university.title: Heap Sort (University)
university.short_summary: Heap sort offers O(n log n) sorting with in-place memory usage by leveraging binary heaps.
university.long_summary: Heap sort first heapifies the array, then repeatedly swaps the root with the last element and heapifies the reduced heap until sorted.
university.algorithm_definition: Build a max-heap from the array and repeatedly extract the maximum to construct the sorted suffix.
university.technical_description: Use sift-down operations to maintain heap property; heapify runs in O(n) and each extraction costs O(log n).
university.application: Used where memory constraints forbid mergesort and where predictable O(n log n) time beats quicksort worst cases.
university.step_by_step: 1) Heapify array. 2) Swap root with last element. 3) Reduce heap size. 4) Sift-down new root. 5) Repeat.

school.title: Dijkstra's Algorithm
school.short_summary: Finds the shortest paths from one node to all others using edge weights.
school.long_summary: Dijkstra's algorithm explores nodes in order of increasing distance and relaxes outgoing edges to maintain best-known paths.
school.simple_explanation: Keep a growing cloud of nodes with known best distances and always expand the cheapest frontier node.
school.where_its_used: Used in GPS navigation, network routing, and resource planning.
school.example: Computing quickest driving directions between two cities.

university.title: Dijkstra's Algorithm (University)
university.short_summary: Dijkstra's algorithm maintains a priority queue of frontier nodes ordered by tentative distance.
university.long_summary: Initialize source distance to zero, push into a min-heap, repeatedly extract the closest node, and relax its outgoing edges if shorter paths are found.
university.algorithm_definition: For weighted graphs with non-negative weights, Dijkstra returns shortest path distances from the source to every vertex.
university.technical_description: Uses a binary or Fibonacci heap to achieve O((V + E) log V) complexity; each relaxation updates the heap key.
university.application: Routing protocols (OSPF), game AI pathfinding, pipeline scheduling.
university.step_by_step: 1) Distance[source]=0. 2) Push source to PQ. 3) Pop min node u. 4) For each edge (u,v,w) relax v. 5) Repeat until PQ empty.
